The Game

GTA VI at a Glance

Grand Theft Auto VI is the latest mainline entry in Rockstar Games' open-world series, and it takes the action back to familiar ground: Vice City. This time, though, the city is only the centre of a much larger state called Leonida — a sun-soaked patchwork of beaches, swamps, small towns, highways and island chains inspired by Florida. Where earlier games gave you one city, GTA VI gives you a whole state to explore, rob and race through.

You play as two protagonists whose lives collide: Lucia Caminos, fresh out of prison and determined never to go back to having nothing, and Jason Duval, a Leonida local who works for the kind of people who pay in cash. Their story is a modern crime saga of trust, ambition and bad decisions — and the game lets you live it from both sides. If you are new to the series, our beginner tips for starting in Vice City will get you comfortable with the controls, the wanted system and your first hours in Leonida.

Everything on this site is written by fans, for fans. We cover the story and characters, break down every major location in our Leonida map guide, catalogue the vehicles you will be stealing, and explain the money-making basics that fund your life of crime. Start with the guides, and welcome to Leonida.

Release & Platforms

Out Now on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S

Grand Theft Auto VI launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar built the game from the ground up for current-generation hardware, which shows in the density of Vice City's streets, the seamless interiors, the wildlife in the Leonida wetlands and the way crowds react to whatever chaos you cause. There is no PlayStation 4 or Xbox One version — the scale of Leonida simply would not fit on the older machines.

Rockstar has not announced a PC version, so if you want to play today, a PS5 or an Xbox Series X|S is the way in. The game is sold through the official PlayStation Store and Xbox Store, as well as at regular game retailers. Be wary of any website offering a "GTA 6 APK", a PC download or a free copy: none of those are legitimate, and Rockstar only distributes the game through official channels. You can read more about editions and what is included further down this page.

Story & Characters

Lucia and Jason: A Leonida Love Story, With Guns

The heart of GTA VI is the relationship between its two leads. Lucia Caminos grew up hard, did time at Leonida Penitentiary, and walks out of the gates with a plan: she and the people she loves are never going to be poor again. Jason Duval grew up around grifters and smugglers in the Leonida Keys, tried the straight life in the army, and came home to work for local drug runners out of a house in Vice City. When a job the two of them pull together goes sideways, they are thrown into a conspiracy that stretches across the whole state — and the only way out is to rely on each other completely.

Around them, Rockstar has built a supporting cast of fixers, smugglers, washed-up music producers, conspiracy theorists and small-town sheriffs, each anchoring a different corner of Leonida. Our Lucia and Jason character guide goes deeper on both protagonists — their backgrounds, how character switching works, and how each of them plays differently in missions and free roam.

The World

Exploring the State of Leonida

Leonida is the biggest map Rockstar has ever made, and it is built to be explored slowly. Vice City itself is the glittering centre: neon beachfronts, art deco hotels, marinas full of yachts, downtown towers and neighbourhoods that change character block by block. South of the city, the Leonida Keys string out into the ocean — laid-back islands of stilt houses, boat yards and smugglers' coves connected by long causeways.

Head north and west and the state changes completely. Port Gellhorn is a faded coastal strip of motels, arcades and boarded-up attractions where the tourists stopped coming years ago. Ambrosia, in the heartland, is industrial country — sugar fields, refineries and biker territory. And on the northern border, Mount Kalaga rises out of the wilderness: forested ridges, hiking trails and wildlife far from the neon. Our map and locations guide walks through every region, what you will find there, and the best ways to get around.

Gameplay

Dual Protagonists, Heists, Wheels and Everything After

GTA VI builds on everything the series does best. The dual-protagonist structure means you can switch between Lucia and Jason as the story demands — and out in the open world, whoever you are not controlling is living their own life somewhere in Leonida. Missions lean into the pair's partnership: robberies planned together, getaways where one drives and the other shoots, and scores that go wrong in ways only the two of them can fix together. The heist fantasy runs through the whole game, from convenience-store stick-ups to carefully planned hits.

Between missions, Leonida is a playground. The vehicle roster covers everything from classic muscle cars and lowriders to speedboats, seaplanes, airboats and dirt bikes, and customisation lets you make them your own. Activities fill every corner of the map: street races, fishing, hunting in the Kalaga wilderness, underground fight clubs, property and business ventures, and a social-media-obsessed world that films your crimes and posts them for the whole state to see. Earning the cash to enjoy it all is its own skill — our money-making basics guide explains where the money is in Leonida and how to keep it.

Editions

Which Edition Should You Buy?

Grand Theft Auto VI is sold in a standard edition containing the full game, and Rockstar and retailers have also offered premium editions bundling extras such as bonus in-game content and collectible items. Edition line-ups, bonus contents and prices can differ between the PlayStation Store, the Xbox Store and physical retailers, and they can change over time — so before you buy, compare the exact contents on the official store pages linked at the top of this page.

Our honest advice for most players: the standard edition contains the complete story and the full open world, and nothing in the premium bundles is required to enjoy Leonida. Choose a premium edition only if you specifically want the extras it lists. Whatever you buy, buy it from an official store — third-party "download" sites are never legitimate sources for this game.

Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

What platforms is GTA VI available on?

Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar has not announced a PC version or versions for older consoles. The safest place to check for any platform news is the official Rockstar Games website.

Who are the main characters in GTA VI?

The story follows two protagonists: Lucia Caminos, who starts the game leaving Leonida Penitentiary, and Jason Duval, who lives and works in Vice City. You play as both across the campaign. See our character guide for the full breakdown.

Where is GTA VI set?

The game is set in the fictional US state of Leonida, which includes Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and the Mount Kalaga region. Our map and locations guide covers each area in detail.

Where can I buy GTA VI safely?

Only from official channels: the PlayStation Store, the Xbox Store, Rockstar's own website, or an established game retailer. Never download the game from third-party sites offering APKs or "free PC versions" — those are not legitimate and are a common source of malware.

Beginner Tips for Starting in Vice City

Your first hours in Leonida set the tone for everything that follows. These practical tips will help you learn the city, stay alive, and avoid the mistakes almost every new player makes.

Take the Opening Hours Slowly

Grand Theft Auto VI opens by introducing Lucia and Jason, their corner of Leonida, and the basics of movement, driving and combat. It is tempting to sprint through these missions to "get to the open world", but the early story does quiet, important work: it teaches you how character switching feels, how the wanted system escalates, and where your first safehouses, shops and garages are. Play the opening at a walking pace. Talk to people, read the phone messages the game sends you, and let the tutorials land. Players who rush the first two hours usually spend the next ten re-learning systems the game already tried to teach them.

Learn the Wanted System Early

Leonida's law enforcement is smarter about witnesses than in older games. Crimes committed in view of bystanders get reported, people film you on their phones, and the police response scales with what you actually did. The beginner-friendly rule is simple: small crimes in quiet places are easy to walk away from, while anything loud in a busy Vice City street brings heat fast. When the stars appear, break line of sight first and change your appearance or vehicle second — swapping cars in an alley or ducking into an interior does more for you than a long highway chase. And if a job is going badly, sometimes the smartest move is to leave the area entirely and let things cool down rather than fighting waves of officers.

Your Phone Is Your Mission Hub

As in modern life, everything in Leonida runs through your phone. Contacts call with work, messages flag side activities, the map app marks your properties, and the in-game social feeds react to the chaos you cause around the state. Get into the habit of checking your phone whenever a mission ends: new opportunities usually arrive quietly, and several of the best early money-makers (covered in our money-making basics guide) begin as a text you could easily miss. The phone is also where you manage contacts for both protagonists, so check it after every character switch.

Drive Like the Car Matters

Early on, you will not own much, and the car you are driving is often the most valuable thing you have. Treat driving as a skill to build rather than a gap between missions. Learn how different vehicle classes handle — a heavy muscle car, a nimble sports coupe and a pickup on a dirt road in Ambrosia are three different games — and practise braking before corners instead of sliding through them. A clean getaway in a car you kept intact beats a spectacular crash every time. When you find a car you love, store it properly in a garage rather than leaving it on the street; our vehicles guide explains garages and customisation in detail.

Spend Your First Money on the Basics

New players tend to blow their first real payout on a flashy car. Resist. Your early cash works harder when it buys capability: body armour before big jobs, a reliable everyday vehicle, weapon upgrades you will actually use, and a buffer so a failed mission or an impounded car is an annoyance rather than a disaster. Vice City is full of expensive temptations, and all of them will still be there later, when the story scores start paying properly. Think of the first act of the game as building your foundation — the luxuries come once Lucia and Jason's operation is actually running.

Explore on Foot, and Talk to the World

Leonida rewards curiosity more than any previous map in the series. Random encounters, small robberies, hidden cash, photo opportunities and strange locals are scattered through every region, and many of them only trigger when you slow down and walk. Get out of the car in new neighbourhoods. Walk the Vice City beachfront at different times of day, wander Port Gellhorn's faded strip, and take a boat around the Keys just to see what is out there. The map and locations guide will help you plan those trips — but leave room in every session for one unplanned detour. That is where this game hides its best stories.

Lucia & Jason: Character Guide

Grand Theft Auto VI is built around two people and the trust between them. Here is who Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval are, how they play, and how to get the most out of controlling both.

Lucia Caminos: Out of Leonida Penitentiary

Lucia Caminos is the first protagonist you meet, and her release from Leonida Penitentiary is where the story begins. She grew up in Liberty City in a family that taught her to fight for what she wanted, and that upbringing carried a price: the skills that kept her safe also put her behind bars. She walks out of prison with a clear-eyed plan — a fresh start, real money, and a better life for the people she loves, achieved the only way she has ever seen work. Lucia is the planner of the pair: focused, disciplined and unwilling to let bad luck write her story twice. In play, she tends to anchor the more deliberate parts of the campaign — the preparation, the negotiation, the moments where keeping a cool head matters more than firepower.

Jason Duval: A Leonida Local

Jason Duval is Leonida born and raised. He grew up around grifters and smugglers in the Keys, enlisted in the army looking for a way out, and came home to find the old life waiting for him. He lives in a house in Vice City provided by the local drug runners he works for, running product and errands while telling himself it is temporary. Jason wants an easy life but keeps choosing the hard road — and meeting Lucia is the moment his story stops drifting. He knows the state the way only a local can: the back roads of Ambrosia, the boat channels of the Keys, who to call in Port Gellhorn and who to avoid. In missions, Jason's local knowledge and driving are the pair's escape route; in free roam, he is your natural guide to the Leonida beyond Vice City, which our map guide explores region by region.

A Partnership, Not a Duo of Strangers

What makes GTA VI's structure different from earlier multi-protagonist games is that Lucia and Jason are a couple, and the story is about their relationship as much as their crimes. Rockstar has described their dynamic as a modern Bonnie-and-Clyde story: two people whose loyalty to each other is the strongest thing in their lives, tested by a conspiracy that keeps pulling them deeper. Missions regularly put them together — planning scores, covering each other, arguing about the next move — and their dialogue out in the world changes as the story develops. Pay attention to the small moments: car conversations, phone calls and the way each of them reacts to the other's decisions carry as much story as the big set pieces.

How Character Switching Works

The campaign directs you to play specific characters for specific story beats, but in free roam you can switch between Lucia and Jason, and the game makes the switch feel alive: the character you leave behind continues their day in Leonida, and you may find them mid-errand, mid-argument or mid-trouble when you return. A few practical habits help. First, switch deliberately before big free-roam plans — starting a long trip or a shopping run as the character whose safehouse, vehicle and contacts suit the job saves backtracking. Second, keep both characters reasonably equipped; a mission can hand you control of either lead at short notice, and the one you neglected will be the one holding the cheap pistol. Third, remember their worlds differ: each has their own contacts, safehouses and side opportunities, so alternating regularly shows you more of the game than mainlining one character.

The People Around Them

Leonida is populated through the pair's extended circle. In the Keys and Vice City you will meet the smugglers and fixers Jason grew up around, the friends and family Lucia is building her new life for, and the ambitious, unreliable operators who see the couple as an opportunity. Further out, Ambrosia's industrial crews, Port Gellhorn's faded hustlers and the state's endless supply of influencers and conspiracy theorists all feed missions and side stories. You do not need to memorise the whole cast — the game reintroduces people naturally — but it is worth reading the messages and background details the game gives you. In GTA VI, knowing who owes whom, and who is lying, is often the difference between a score that pays and one that explodes. If you are just starting out, pair this guide with our beginner tips for the systems side of the opening hours.

Next step: learn the state they call home in our Leonida map and locations guide.

Leonida Map & Locations Guide

Leonida is a whole state, not just a city — beaches and boardwalks, swamps and sugar country, island chains and a mountain border. Here is how its regions fit together and what each one is for.

Vice City: The Neon Heart

Vice City sits on Leonida's south-eastern coast and remains the state's beating heart. The beachfront districts are the postcard version — pastel art deco hotels, crowded sand, marinas and Ocean Drive-style neon — while downtown brings towers, offices and money, and the neighbourhoods inland shift from wealthy suburbs to working blocks where Lucia and Jason's story actually lives. Vice City is where you will spend the most time: it holds the densest shops, services, garages, activities and mission-givers, and its street grid is worth learning properly. A practical approach for new players is to learn one neighbourhood at a time, using the beachfront as your compass — the ocean is always east. When the wanted level rises, the city's alleys, interiors and parking structures are your best friends, as covered in our beginner tips.

The Leonida Keys: Islands and Smugglers' Water

South-west of the city, a chain of low islands strings out into the ocean, connected by long causeways that are some of the best drives in the game. The Keys are slower than Vice City: stilt houses, fish shacks, boat yards, dive bars and marinas, with a local economy that mixes tourism and the kind of cargo nobody declares. This is Jason's home turf, and the region plays to water as much as road — boats are essential transport here, not a novelty. Bring a fast car for the causeways, but plan to explore by boat: the channels, sandbars and little coves between islands hide encounters and shortcuts you will never see from the highway. At sunset, the drive back toward the city skyline is the single best view in Leonida.

Port Gellhorn: The Faded Strip

On the western coast, Port Gellhorn is where Leonida's tourist boom went to fade. Its strip of motels, arcades, mini-golf and boarded attractions has seen better decades, and the people who remain are a mix of lifers, drifters and hustlers working the angles that are left. Do not mistake the peeling paint for emptiness: Port Gellhorn is dense with side characters and odd jobs, and its cheaper, quieter streets make it a useful place to lie low, stash vehicles and do business away from Vice City's cameras. It is also a good early-game base for earning money without heavy police attention, precisely because nobody important is watching.

Ambrosia: Sugar, Smoke and Industry

Inland Leonida is Ambrosia country: flat fields of sugar cane, refineries, rail lines and small industrial towns where the refinery whistle sets the schedule. This is the state's working heartland and its biker territory — expect long straight roads, heavy trucks, dirt tracks and a very different pace from the coast. Ambrosia matters in play because it is where a lot of Leonida's goods are made and moved; missions and side work here lean on trucking, rural getaways and knowing which dirt road connects to which highway. Off-road vehicles earn their keep in Ambrosia, and the region's emptiness cuts both ways: fewer witnesses, but also fewer places to hide when something goes wrong.

Mount Kalaga: The Wild Border

On Leonida's northern edge, the flatlands give way to the forested ridges of Mount Kalaga, a wilderness region of trails, rivers, wildlife and small mountain communities. Kalaga is the state's escape hatch — the place to hunt, hike, ride dirt bikes and disappear. It is also genuinely remote: services are sparse, the weather turns, and a breakdown or a wrecked vehicle is a real problem, so arrive prepared and fuelled. For explorers, Kalaga offers the strongest contrast in the game; after hours under Vice City neon, standing on a ridge at dawn with the whole state below you is the moment the map's scale really lands. Our vehicles guide covers the off-road choices that make Kalaga trips easier.

Getting Around a Very Big State

Leonida is large enough that travel is a decision, not an afterthought. Highways and causeways move you between regions quickly; boats own the Keys and the coast; aircraft, once you have access, turn cross-state trips into minutes. Build a personal network as you play: a reliable car garaged in Vice City, a boat you can reach in the Keys, an off-roader for Ambrosia and Kalaga. Learn the handful of bridges and causeways that connect everything — they are chokepoints for police and shortcuts for you, depending on the day. Most of all, travel with your eyes open: Leonida's random encounters happen on the road, and the detour you almost skipped is often the best thing in the session.

Vehicles Guide

In Leonida, your vehicle is your tool, your weapon and your escape plan. How the vehicle classes work, what customisation is worth paying for, and how to build a collection that covers the whole state.

The Classes That Matter

GTA VI's vehicle roster spans the full Leonida lifestyle, but for practical play it helps to think in roles rather than model names. Everyday cars — sedans, hatchbacks and coupes — are anonymous, cheap to replace and perfect for moving around Vice City without attention. Sports and super cars own the highways and causeways: devastating in a straight line, expensive to buy and repair, and memorable to every witness. Muscle cars deliver the classic Vice City fantasy with strong acceleration and loose rear ends that reward practice. SUVs and pickups are the state's workhorses, trading speed for toughness and cargo sense. Motorcycles are the fastest way through city traffic and the most dangerous way to crash. And beyond the roads, boats rule the Keys and coastline while aircraft — planes and helicopters — turn Leonida's size into a non-issue once you can access them.

Match the Vehicle to the Job

The most common vehicle mistake in GTA VI is bringing a favourite instead of the right tool. A supercar is a liability on Ambrosia dirt and a death sentence on Mount Kalaga trails; a lifted pickup is wasted on a downtown tailing mission where a grey sedan disappears into traffic. Before any planned job, ask three questions: How fast do I need to leave? How much attention can I afford? What terrain sits between me and safety? Robberies in the city want something quick and forgettable parked around the corner. Rural work wants ground clearance and durability. Anything in the Keys wants a boat plan as well as a road plan. Players who build this habit — also emphasised in our beginner tips — fail fewer missions and spend far less replacing wrecked cars.

Customisation: Performance First, Looks Second

Leonida's mod shops let you reshape a vehicle inside and out, and the temptation is to spend on paint and wheels first. Do it the other way around. Performance upgrades — engine, brakes, transmission, suspension and tyres — change what a vehicle can actually do, and brakes in particular are the unglamorous upgrade that wins chases, because the player who can brake later and turn cleaner escapes more often than the player with the higher top speed. Armour and durability options earn their price on any vehicle you use for work. Cosmetics absolutely have their place — this is Vice City, and arriving in style is half the culture — but style a car you have already made good. Keep one fully personalised "signature" vehicle per protagonist for free-roam joy, and keep your working vehicles purposeful.

Garages, Storage and Keeping What You Steal

A vehicle you cannot store is a vehicle you will lose. Properties and safehouses come with garage space, and owned vehicles stored properly are the backbone of your Leonida life: insured against the chaos, waiting where you left them, ready in the spec you built. Early on, garage space is limited, so be selective — store vehicles that fill roles (a daily driver, a fast escape car, an off-roader) rather than five near-identical coupes. As your money grows, expand storage in the regions where you actually operate; a boat accessible in the Keys and an off-roader waiting near Ambrosia save more time than a tenth sports car in a Vice City garage. Details on funding all of this are in the money-making basics guide.

Boats and Aircraft Deserve Respect

New players often treat water and air as minigames. In Leonida they are core transport. The Keys are designed around boats: missions, smuggling routes and escapes all assume you can handle channels, shallows and open water, and a fast centre-console boat is one of the best purchases in the game. Aircraft change your relationship with the map entirely — seaplanes suit the coast and Keys beautifully, helicopters make Mount Kalaga and downtown rooftops accessible, and both turn cross-state travel into a pleasure instead of a commute. Practise landings somewhere forgiving before you need one under pressure. The water off Port Gellhorn has taught a lot of pilots humility.

Stealing Smart

Finally, the series' namesake skill. Taking vehicles is easy; taking them well is an art. Quiet streets, distracted owners and distance from patrols matter more than the car itself. High-end cars in wealthy Vice City districts pay off in fun but draw attention, while the humble car taken cleanly gets you home. Remember that a stolen car carries its own heat — if the police are looking for the vehicle, your driving is irrelevant. Swap into something clean when the pressure is on, and let the hot car go. It is only metal; Lucia and Jason are the irreplaceable part of every getaway.

Money-Making Basics in GTA VI

Everything in Leonida costs money — cars, guns, property, style. This guide explains how cash actually flows through GTA VI, and the habits that turn a broke start into a funded operation.

How Money Works in Leonida

Cash in GTA VI comes from four broad sources: the story, side work, the world itself, and property or business income. The story pays in big, irregular lump sums — scores and major jobs that land like paydays and then stop. Side work pays smaller amounts steadily: errands for contacts, local hustles, races and the endless small opportunities Leonida generates. The world pays opportunistically — cash in registers, valuables in the right (wrong) places, encounters that turn profitable. And once you own them, properties and businesses convert your money into more money over time. Understanding this rhythm matters: early on you live off side work and small opportunities, the story funds your growth in jumps, and late-game income is about owning things. Players who grasp which phase they are in stop feeling broke, because they stop expecting the wrong source to pay.

The Early Game: Small Money, Done Often

At the start, Lucia and Jason have skills and problems, but no capital. The early money game is volume: take the small jobs your contacts offer, complete the quick opportunities your phone flags, and treat every few hundred dollars as meaningful — because it is. This is also when spending discipline matters most, as our beginner tips explain: armour, a dependable car and a cash buffer beat luxuries. Avoid two early traps. The first is grinding one repetitive activity until the game stops being fun; Leonida offers enough variety that rotating activities pays nearly as well and plays far better. The second is gambling your stake on long-shot schemes before you can afford the loss. Build the buffer first. In Leonida, the player with reserves can walk away from bad deals — and walking away is a money-making skill.

Story Scores: Prepare Like It Matters

The campaign's big jobs are where real money moves, and they reward the habits this site keeps recommending: preparation, the right vehicle, and knowing your escape geography. Before a major score, stock armour and ammunition, position a suitable getaway vehicle (the vehicles guide covers choosing one), and scout the route to safety in free roam while nobody is chasing you. During the job, greed is the tax: optional loot that costs time under police pressure often costs more than it pays. After the job, resist the victory spending spree for one in-game day — let the heat die, see what the story takes from you, and then invest deliberately. Treated this way, each story payday permanently upgrades your operation instead of evaporating into a weekend in Vice City.

Side Work and the Leonida Hustle

Between scores, side work is your salary. Leonida generates it constantly: contact missions, local requests in each region, races with entry fees and prizes, recovery and delivery jobs, and the ambient criminal economy of stick-ups and opportunistic theft. Regional variety helps your wallet as well as your interest — Port Gellhorn's low-attention hustles, Ambrosia's hauling and rural work, the Keys' boat-based jobs and Vice City's dense mission board each pay in their own rhythm. Keep both protagonists' contact lists active, since Lucia and Jason draw different work, and finish what you start: many chains of side jobs escalate, and the third job for a contact usually pays better than the first.

Property and Businesses: Money That Works While You Play

Once your capital allows it, property changes your financial life. Businesses and income properties in Leonida generate returns over time and unlock their own mission chains, which in turn pay again — the closest thing the game has to compound interest. Buy with your play style, not just the brochure: a business in a region you enjoy, running jobs you like doing, outperforms a theoretically optimal purchase you never visit. Keep operating costs and required attention in mind, expand one solid holding before scattering money across three weak ones, and remember that property also stores value practically — garages and safehouses across the state are quality-of-life purchases that pay you back in saved time every session, as the map guide describes.

Spending Rules for Staying Rich

Getting money in GTA VI is the fun half; keeping it is a system. Four rules cover most of it. Keep a reserve you do not touch except for genuine emergencies — hospital bills, lost vehicles and failed jobs are Leonida certainties. Buy capability before cosmetics, always: the upgraded brakes and the second garage move your game forward, the third paint job does not. Match purchases to income phase — do not buy late-game luxuries on early-game money. And finally, insure and store what matters, because the most expensive vehicle in Leonida is the uninsured one at the bottom of the bay. Follow those rules and the money system stops being a wall and becomes what it should be: the engine of your life in Leonida.

New to all of this? Start with our beginner tips for starting in Vice City.

Home · FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

The questions players ask most about Grand Theft Auto VI and about this site, answered in one place.

What platforms is GTA VI available on?

Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. There is no PlayStation 4 or Xbox One version, and Rockstar has not announced a PC version. Any platform announcements will come from Rockstar Games directly.

Who do you play as in GTA VI?

You play as two protagonists: Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a couple whose story unfolds across the state of Leonida. The campaign switches between them, and in free roam you can choose who to control. Our character guide covers both in depth.

Where is GTA VI set?

In Leonida, a fictional state inspired by Florida. Its major locations include Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and the Mount Kalaga wilderness. See the map and locations guide for the full tour.

Is GTA VI a sequel to GTA V?

It is the next mainline Grand Theft Auto game, with its own setting, story and protagonists. It returns the series to Vice City, which last headlined a game in Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, in a modern-day setting.

Where can I buy GTA VI safely?

From official channels only: the PlayStation Store, the Xbox Store, rockstargames.com, or an established game retailer. Never use sites offering APK downloads, "free" copies or PC installers — the game is not distributed that way.

Can I download GTA VI from this website?

No. GTA 6 Hub is a guide site only. We host no downloads of any kind — no game files, no APKs, no mods. Our "get the game" links point exclusively to official stores.

Is GTA 6 Hub an official Rockstar site?

No. This is an unofficial fan site, not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive. Grand Theft Auto and GTA are trademarks of Take-Two Interactive. See our disclaimer.

Which guide should I read first?

If you are new to the game, start with Beginner Tips for Starting in Vice City, then Money-Making Basics. Returning players usually head straight for the map guide and the vehicles guide. All five are listed on the guides page.

How can I contact GTA 6 Hub?

Through the contact page, or by email at contact@gtavihub.github.io.
